prompt:
An electric car of mass 1350 kg accelerates uniformly from an initial speed of 12.0 m s^-1 to a final speed of 24.0 m s^-1 along a straight horizontal track in a time of 5.00 s.
(a) Calculate the gain in kinetic energy of the car. [2]
(b) Calculate the average net power required to cause this acceleration. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates Delta E_k = 2.92 * 10^5 J (accept 2.916 * 10^5 J or 292 kJ).
Calculates average net power P = Delta E_k / t = 2.916 * 10^5 / 5.00 = 5.83 * 10^4 W (or 58.3 kW).

hints: In part (a), calculate final kinetic energy and initial kinetic energy, then subtract: Delta E_k = (1/2)m(v^2 - u^2).
In part (b), power is the rate of energy transfer: P = Delta E_k / t.
solution:
(a) Initial kinetic energy E_k1 = 0.5 * 1350 * (12.0)^2 = 675 * 144 = 97 200 J.
Final kinetic energy E_k2 = 0.5 * 1350 * (24.0)^2 = 675 * 576 = 388 800 J.
Gain in kinetic energy Delta E_k = 388 800 - 97 200 = 291 600 J = 2.92 * 10^5 J (or 292 kJ).
(b) Average net power P = Delta E_k / t = 291 600 J / 5.00 s = 58 320 W = 5.83 * 10^4 W (or 58.3 kW).
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Award C1 for formula and substitution of both speeds squared. Award A1 for 2.92 * 10^5 J.
Note: Warning students against squaring the difference (24 - 12)^2 = 144, which gives an incorrect value of 97.2 kJ.
Check that answers are given to 3 significant figures.
